title: High-throughput usage onramp with progressive schema fuzz mitigation
creator: Priya Nambiar
description:
Background: Our usage pipeline sees a growing diversity of event shapes as new SDKs, partner integrations, and versioned clients roll out. Current strict-validate-or-drop behavior causes transient user-visible telemetry loss and noisy operator alerts. Goal: introduce a high-throughput "onramp" service that performs fast-path syntactic validation, progressive schema fuzz mitigation, and quarantining for odd payloads so we can preserve signal while minimizing downstream pipeline failures.

Scope and approach:
- Implement a lightweight ingress verifier written in Go that runs ahead of the main ingest fleet. The verifier enforces required top-level fields, content-type sanity, and token-limited payload size checks.
- Add a progressive fuzz-mitigation layer: policy-driven ruleset that (a) auto-fills missing low-risk fields with sentinel values, (b) coerces string/number types when obvious, and (c) marks events with a "fuzz_score" header for downstream scoring.
- Quarantine path: events that fail critical validation but appear recoverable are routed to a quarantine Kafka topic for offline repair and reingest. Events that are clearly corrupted are rejected with a structured error returned to the SDK/client.
- Backpressure and shedding: integrate ingress verifier with rate and CPU signals to perform smart shedding under overload; prefer quarantining non-critical events rather than dropping.
- Observability: emit per-event validation reason, fuzz_score histogram, quarantine ratio, and downstream recovery rate to the console analytics dashboards.

Acceptance criteria:
1) End-to-end p99 ingestion latency added by the verifier < 6 ms at steady-state.
2) Overall downstream pipeline error rate due to schema failures reduced by >= 65% on canary customers.
3) Quarantine + repair pipeline demonstrates >= 40% successful auto-repair reingest rate within 24 hours on canary traffic.
4) New metrics surfaced in Console: "ingest.verifier.latency_ms", "ingest.verifier.fuzz_score", "ingest.quarantine.rate", and a sample payload link for forensic debugging.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Auto-coercion reduces signal purity and may mask client bugs; mitigated by conservative default policies and exposing fuzz_score prominently so product teams can gate features on high-confidence data only.
- Quarantine storage growth under surge; mitigated by TTL and prioritized repair jobs.
- Performance overhead of per-event scoring; designed as fast-path heuristics in native code with optional sampling for deep scoring.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1: Internal canary (10% of internal telemetry) for performance and metric validation.
- Phase 2: Partner canary for 3 selected customers with diverse SDKs.
- Phase 3: Gradual ramp with 1-day hold windows and automated rollback on SLO regression.

Dependencies: ENG-71298, ENG-47059, ENG-43106

Customer impact: medium

Release: console-2026.03

Security review required: true
